note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Acute diarrheal illness with central abdominal pain and vomiting for 3 days; clinical impression: likely gastroenteritis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Diarrhea for 3 days with central (periumbilical/suprapubic) abdominal pain and recent vomiting (last vomit this morning).
- Symptom course: Patient reports symptoms started 3 days ago and have neither improved nor worsened.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Urgency/frequent bowel motions (needs to be near a toilet; reports feeling of needing to go again soon after defecation).
  - Nausea; one episode of vomiting this morning (thought to be partially vomited fruit).
  - Patient reports hearing stomach noises.
  - Mild sweating over last four days; patient uncertain if this represented fever.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - Patient reports no blood in stool.
  - No chest pain.
  - No new or worsening breathing apart from baseline asthma.
- Past medical history:
  - Asthma.
- Allergies:
  - Patient states "NKDA" (no known drug allergies) as reported in the consult.
- Medications:
  - Inhaler for asthma (new inhaler recently obtained; prior inhaler had run out). Dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Patient reports using inhaler more when anxious.
- Family history:
  - Father died ~10 years ago of bowel cancer; patient concerned about cancer risk.
- Social / other:
  - Patient is a foreign national (patient statement).
  - Currently limiting activities and not attending work due to need for frequent toilet access.
  - Ambulation limited by need to be near toilet.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Abdominal examination: patient reports mild pain on palpation of the central abdomen ("does a little bit" when pressed).
- Other examination findings: none documented.

Impression:
- Working diagnosis: likely gastroenteritis (infectious diarrheal illness) as per clinician assessment.

Plan:
- Supportive management advised:
  - Oral rehydration: increase fluid intake (drink lots of water/fluids).
  - Symptom monitoring: watch for development of fever or clinical worsening.
  - Stay home/avoid work while symptomatic until improvement.
  - Avoid antibiotics (not recommended routinely for this presentation).
- Safety-netting / follow-up:
  - If symptoms significantly worsen or do not improve, patient advised to see GP in person for abdominal examination.
  - Patient intends to wait 1–2 days and then book with GP if not improved.
- Reassurance:
  - Clinician advised presentation is more suggestive of an acute infection than of the bowel cancer seen in the patient's father; further evaluation can be arranged by GP if symptoms persist or worsen.

document_quality (Quality checks):
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective vital signs (temperature, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate).
  - Quantitative stool frequency/volume and stool consistency details.
  - Objective assessment of dehydration.
  - Formal abdominal exam findings documented by clinician (tenderness location/severity, guarding, rebound).
  - Exact inhaler name, dose, route and frequency; complete medication list.
  - Clarification of allergy status (patient stated "NKDA" but wording was fragmented).
  - Recent travel, food exposures, recent antibiotic use, and immunization status not documented.
  - Urinalysis, blood tests, or stool studies not documented (if considered).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Conflict noted: patient initially gave date of birth as 1/1/1992 but later stated age 48 (inconsistent).
- Transcript quality comment:
  - Audio/transcript generally intelligible though patient occasionally hesitated and corrected information; some repetition and minor ambiguity about allergies and dates. Overall sufficient to document presenting complaint and plan.
